strategy.observation: Stripe supports usage-based billing, charging customers according to their service consumption during a billing period.
strategy.offer_link: Localizing the developer documentation for usage-based billing into Japanese, German and Brazilian Portuguese could help developers who prefer those languages understand and implement consumption-based charging, if Stripe has coverage gaps in those languages.
hypotheses: Some developers implementing Stripe’s usage-based billing may prefer documentation in Japanese, German or Brazilian Portuguese.
The relevant documentation may have gaps in coverage or freshness in those languages; the facts do not establish its current localization status.
The Head of Documentation may prioritize making technical billing guidance accessible across languages.
strategy.angle: Does Stripe’s usage-based billing documentation have any Japanese, German or Brazilian Portuguese coverage gaps you’re looking to close?
strategy.fit_reason: The offer directly concerns developer documentation and the recipient’s remit, with usage-based billing providing a concrete scope for localization. Actual demand depends on language coverage and developer needs, neither of which is confirmed.

draft.subject: Language coverage for usage-based billing docs
draft.body:
Hi,

Are there any gaps in Stripe’s usage-based billing documentation in Japanese, German or Brazilian Portuguese that you’re looking to close?

I localize developer documentation into those three languages. If developers implementing consumption-based charging prefer to work in one of them, having the relevant guidance available could make implementation easier.

I don’t know where your coverage stands today, so I’d start with a narrow scope rather than a broader documentation project. Is there one usage-based billing guide you’d prioritize for localization into one of those languages?
